answer: Escrowing non-transferable tokens in time-locked fidelity bonds forces every agent key to keep principal locked across multiple epochs, with contracts slashing deposits if fraud proofs show equivocation. Each concurrent Sybil therefore incurs linear capital lockup and foregone yield. The drawback is wealth bias: rich adversaries can still fund compliant clones, while low-margin nodes like a prism sensor assaying copper in basalt strata get priced out.
